# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Sawyer Alvarez
**Member ID:** W635441117
**Reference Number:** POC-A1F3D3C000-86797
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-11
**Governing Policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty (effective 3/15/2026), https://static.cigna.com/assets/chcp/pdf/coveragePolicies/medical/mm_0285_coveragepositioncriteria_total_ankle_arthroplasty.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which I received in a notice dated 2026-08-11. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I believe the records show that my case meets the plan's own published criteria.

## Why I believe this denial should be reconsidered

The denial notice lists several criteria "at issue," but many of them concern **revision** total ankle arthroplasty — that is, replacing an ankle implant that has already failed. For example, the policy states:

> "0285 Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for moderate to severe ankle pain secondary to failure of an implanted device (e.g., implant loosening, malpositioning, periprosthetic infection, periprosthetic fracture)."

and

> "Revision total ankle arthroplasty for any other indication is considered not medically necessary."

My request is for a **primary** total ankle replacement. Nothing in my records indicates that I have a prior ankle implant, so these revision-specific criteria do not appear to apply to my situation. I ask that the reviewer confirm this distinction and evaluate my request under the criteria that actually govern a first-time total ankle replacement.

The policy sets out that criterion as follows:

> "Food and Drug Administration (FDA)- approved/cleared device* is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

> " is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration  interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy) • individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty:"

Here is how my records match each part of that standard:

- **Function-limiting at short distances, for at least three months:** My records document that I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks — which the policy itself gives as an example of this criterion ("limiting activity to two city blocks"). My symptoms have been present and progressive for 12 months, well beyond the three-month threshold.

- **Failure of at least six months of conservative therapy:** My records document NSAID use for 8 months with inadequate relief, a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29 that gave only two weeks of partial relief, and 10 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27 focused on ankle strengthening and balance. This matches the therapies the policy names as conservative management: "medications for pain control, limiting activity, the use of ankle braces to stabilize the joint, shoe modifications, heat, and physical therapy to control the pain associated with ankle arthrosis." My conservative treatment has extended well beyond six months without adequate relief.

- **No contraindications:** My records document no active infection and no untreated substance use. [If the plan's contraindication list includes additional items not listed in the excerpt above, please advise so the record can address each one specifically.]

My imaging also supports the underlying severity of my condition. Weight-bearing radiographs from 2026-06-02 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, and my exam findings include positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain. The policy notes that "[w]hen conservative management fails, ankle arthrodesis (AA) (fusion) has been the standard surgical treatment of choice to control the pain of severe ankle arthritis," and that an FDA-approved device is medically necessary "as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis" when the criteria above are met. My surgeon has determined that total ankle replacement, rather than fusion, is the appropriate option in my case.

## What I am asking

I am asking Cigna to reconsider this denial in light of the policy's own criteria for primary total ankle arthroplasty as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis, and the clinical documentation summarized above. I have asked my surgeon's office to provide any additional records that may help this review, including confirmation of the specific FDA-approved/cleared device proposed. [Placeholder: device name/manufacturer, if required.]

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-07, though I will rely on the deadline printed on my denial letter as authoritative. I plan to submit this appeal by logging in at my.cigna.com to locate my plan's appeal form, or by calling the number on my member ID card (1-800-244-6224), and I will mail it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

[Sawyer Alvarez]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
